## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The short discourse presents a concise doctrinal teaching centered on overcoming the defilement of disdain or contempt (*makkha*): by fully abandoning this single quality, one is assured the spiritual attainment of non-return.

A direct parallel to the sutta is preserved in the Chinese Buddhist canon in the *Itivuttaka* translation at T 765.18 (覆藏).

None of the retrieved secondary reference passages discuss Iti 5 directly; rather, they cite or translate the term *makkha* as a generic psychological defilement (*upakkilesa*) or as one of Māra's armies in other canonical contexts.
